desc:
A pair of indices (i, j) with i < j is identical when nums[i] == nums[j]. Return the number of identical pairs in nums.

For example, [1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 3] has 4 identical pairs: indices (0,3), (0,4), (3,4) and (2,5).
constraints: The answer is at most 49,995,000, so it fits in 32 bits
hints: Checking all pairs works for small inputs. How many pairs does a value that appears c times contribute on its own?
Pairs can only be formed inside a group of equal values, so you can count each group separately.
A value occurring c times gives c * (c - 1) / 2 pairs. Count occurrences with a hash map and add these up (or add the current count each time you see a value again).
editorial: Group equal values with a frequency map. Inside a group of size c every two elements form a pair, so the group contributes c(c-1)/2 pairs; groups of different values never contribute. Summing over all groups gives the answer in O(n).

A one-pass variant keeps a running count per value: when you meet a value that has been seen s times before, it forms exactly s new pairs with those earlier copies, so add s to the total and then increment the count.
